scenes.voiceover: Christmas 2021. A billion-dollar gold mirror launched to see the dawn of time.

content.title: James Webb Space Telescope
content.caption: Christmas Day 2021 — Ariane 5 launches from Kourou

image.alt: Ariane 5 rocket launching the James Webb Space Telescope on Christmas Day 2021

scenes.voiceover: Six times the light of Hubble. Eighteen gold hexagons unfolding in deep space.

content.label: X HUBBLE LIGHT
content.caption: 18 gold hexagons — a 6.5-metre mirror, unfolded at L2

scenes.voiceover: Minus 223 degrees. Five paper-thin shields. SPF one million.

content.label: DEGREES C
content.caption: Five Kapton layers thin as a human hair

scenes.voiceover: July 2022. Webb's first deep field — galaxies thirteen billion years old.

content.title: Webb's First Deep Field
content.caption: SMACS 0723 — galaxies as they were 13.1 billion years ago

image.alt: Webb's First Deep Field — SMACS 0723 galaxy cluster with lensed background galaxies

scenes.voiceover: Then the cosmic cliffs — star birth carved into the Carina Nebula.

image.alt: Cosmic Cliffs of the Carina Nebula — Webb NIRCam image

scenes.voiceover: A dying star's final performance. Southern Ring Nebula, death in infrared.

content.title: Dying Star — Southern Ring
content.caption: 2,500 light-years away — NIRCam and MIRI side by side

image.alt: Southern Ring Nebula NIRCam and MIRI images side by side

scenes.voiceover: One thousand one hundred and twenty light-years away — water vapour on a gas giant.

content.label: LIGHT-YEARS
content.caption: Webb's first exoplanet atmosphere spectrum — water on WASP-96b

scenes.voiceover: Webb sees the universe as it was thirteen billion years ago — the dawn of time, in infrared.

content.quote: We are seeing the universe as it was 13 billion years ago — the dawn of time, in infrared.
content.source: NASA, on Webb's first deep field
content.caption: James Webb Space Telescope — NASA / ESA / CSA
